'''Ana María Cetto Kramis'''{{Family name footnote|Cetto|Kramis|lang=Mexican}} (born 1946) is a Mexican [[physicist]] and professor. Her work specializes in [[quantum mechanics]], stochastic theory, [[electrodynamics]], and biophysics of [[light]]. She is also known for her work as a [[pacifist]] and activist for women in science.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Ana María Cetto, reconocida científica por su labor pacifista {{!}} Fundación UNAM |url=https://www.fundacionunam.org.mx/rostros/ana-maria-cetto-reconocida-cientifica-por-su-labor-pacifista/ |access-date=2022-04-11 |language=es}}</ref> From 2003 to 2010 she was deputy director general of the [[International Atomic Energy Agency]] (IAEA). She was also professor and director at the [[Faculty of Sciences (UNAM)|Faculty of Sciences]] at the [[National Autonomous University of Mexico]] (UNAM), from 1979 to 1982.<ref name=":5" /> Cetto Kramis is responsible for several scientific literature programs in Latin America and for several international programs on the promotion and participation of women in physics.

== Early life ==
Ana María Cetto Kramis was born and raised in [[Mexico City]], attending primary and secondary school in the greater Mexico City area.<ref name=":6" /> She was raised by her parents Gertrud Katarina Kramis, a Swiss designer, and [[Max Cetto]], a German architect. Her parents were refugees from the Nazi dictatorship. She completed her primary schooling at the [[Colegio Alemán Alexander von Humboldt (Mexico City)|German School Alexander von Humboldt of Mexico City]], but requested to be transferred to public high school and attended Secondary School No. 8 (named for [[Tomáš Masaryk|Tomáš Garrigue Masaryk]]), in [[San Pedro de los Pinos]]. Ultimately, she returned to the German School to complete her two-year preparatory education. Her physics courses were conducted in German, which "presented some challenges for her, as she felt it was not the same as thinking in Spanish."<ref name=":9">{{Cite book |url=https://www.cambridge.org/core/product/identifier/9781009535816/type/book |title=Women in the History of Quantum Physics: Beyond Knabenphysik |date=2025-06-19 |publisher=Cambridge University Press |isbn=978-1-009-53581-6 |editor-last=Charbonneau |editor-first=Patrick |edition=1 |doi=10.1017/9781009535816 |editor-last2=Frank |editor-first2=Michelle |editor-last3=van der Heijden |editor-first3=Margriet |editor-last4=Monaldi |editor-first4=Daniela}}</ref>

== Education ==
Ana María Cetto Kramis attended the local [[National Autonomous University of Mexico]] (UNAM) for her undergraduate degree. For graduate school, Cetto Kramis relocated to the United States for a master's degree in biophysics at [[Harvard University]]. She then returned to UNAM where she obtained a master's degree and research PhD focusing on stochastic theory and quantum mechanics. Cetto Kramis more recently gained honorary doctorates from [[Tajik National University|Tajik State National University]] (TSNU) from 2007 and the [[Azerbaijan National Academy of Sciences]] in 2010.<ref name=":4">{{Cite web |title=Nuestra Gente - Dra Ana María Beatriz Cetto Kramis |url=https://www.fisica.unam.mx/es/personal.php?id=168 |access-date=2022-04-11 |website=www.fisica.unam.mx |language=en}}</ref>

==National and international work==
Ana María Cetto Kramis has published over 300 scientific articles on various subjects: stochastic theory, quantum mechanics, and Latin American science advocation. She has also been the director of the Faculty of Sciences at UNAM (1978–1982),<ref>{{Cite web |last=Cavanillas |first=Belen |date=2016-03-16 |title=Entrevista a Doctora Ana María Cetto de UNAM |url=https://smart-lighting.es/contagiar-pasion-la-ciencia-ana-maria-cetto/ |access-date=2022-04-11 |website=smartlighting |language=es}}</ref> as well as a professor, and researcher at the same institution. She was elected president of the executive committee of the [[Mexican Society of Physics]] in 2021.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Cómite Ejecutivo |url=https://smf.mx/nosotros/mesa-directiva/comite-ejecutivo/ |access-date=2022-04-11 |website=Sociedad Mexicana de Física |language=en-US}}</ref>

Cetto Kramis has been involved in the management of several international organizations. In 1995, she was council member of the [[Pugwash Conferences]],<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |date=2016-06-14 |title=Ciencia y género: entrevista a Ana María Cetto • LADO B |url=https://www.ladobe.com.mx/2016/06/ciencia-y-genero-entrevista-a-ana-maria-cetto/ |access-date=2022-04-11 |website=LADO B |language=es}}</ref> and in 2002 she was appointed as general secretary of the [[International Council for Science]] (ICSU), becoming the first Latin American appointed to the position.<ref name=":0" /> Cetto Kramis is also a co-founder and vice-president of the [[Third World Organization for Women in Science]] (TWOWS). From 2003 to 2010 she was Deputy Technical Director of the [[International Atomic Energy Agency]] (IAEA).<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |last=Partnership (IAP) |first=the InterAcademy |title=Ana María Cetto |url=https://www.interacademies.org/person/ana-maria-cetto |access-date=2022-04-11 |website=www.interacademies.org |language=en-GB}}</ref> She has also been a member of the Governing Board of the [[United Nations University]] (UNU) and a counsel president for the [[International Foundation for Science]] (IFS).

Cetto Kramis's trajectory has been recognized on various occasions. She was awarded as "Woman of the Year" in Mexico in 2003 for being an "ambassador of physics in Mexico".<ref>{{Cite web |title="Mujer del año", Ana María Cetto, Julieta Fierro y Linda Manzanilla |url=https://www.proceso.com.mx/nacional/2003/12/10/mujer-del-ano-ana-maria-cetto-julieta-fierro-linda-manzanilla-81088.html |access-date=2022-04-11 |website=www.proceso.com.mx |language=es}}</ref> She has also received several other distinctions as a member of the [[Third World Academy of Science]], the [[Mexican Academy of Sciences]], the Mexican Academy of Physics and the [[American Physical Society]], and as a member of the [[World Future Council]]. Cetto Kramis has held several roles in the [[International Union of Pure and Applied Physics]], among others she was chair of the working group on ethics.<ref>{{Cite web |last=iupap |date=2021-02-17 |title=Ethics, Science Integrity and Collegiality - IUPAP: The International Union of Pure and Applied Physics |url=https://iupap.org/strategic-plan/ethics-and-science-integrity/ |access-date=2026-10-31 |language=en-US}}</ref>

In 2015, the [[University of Guadalajara]] created the "Ana María Cetto Chair for the Diffusion of Scientific Culture" in recognition of her scientific work.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2017-11-30 |title=Cátedra para la Difusión de la Cultura Científica Ana María Cetto {{!}} Coordinación General de Comunicación Social |url=http://comsoc.udg.mx/actividades/catedra-para-la-difusion-de-la-cultura-cientifica-ana-maria-cetto |access-date=2022-04-11 |website=comsoc.udg.mx |language=es}}</ref> Cetto Kramis has also participated in several international programs aimed at promoting women's participation in science.<ref name=":5" /> Because of her advocacy, she received the "Sor Juana Inés de la Cruz" distinction awarded by the UNAM.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Conociendo a Ana María Cetto Kramis. La Mujer Atómica |url=https://www.revistahypatia.org/439 |access-date=2022-04-11 |website=www.revistahypatia.org}}</ref> She is also responsible for the creation of scientific information programs in Latin America, and programs for the promotion and participation of women in science.

Throughout her career, Cetto Kramis has been involved in various initiatives promoting women in science. She is a jury member of the [[Ada Byron Award]], Mexico Chapter,<ref name=":7">{{Cite web |title=Jurado – Premio Ada Byron |url=https://premioadabyron.ibero.mx/jurado/ |access-date=2022-04-11 |language=es}}</ref> an award created by the [[University of Deusto]] to recognize women who work in the fields of science, technology, engineering, and mathematics.<ref name=":7" />

=== Scientific dissemination ===
Another of her lines of work has been the dissemination of scientific content. Cetto Kramis is a directing member of the ''Revista Mexicana de Física'' and the founding president of [[Latindex|Latindex (Regional Online Information System for Scientific Journals from Latin America, the Caribbean, Spain, and Portugal)]]: a free, open-access, online scholarly journal system created in 1997, containing Spanish translations of scholarly sources.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Latindex - Sistema regional de información en línea para Revistas científicas de América Latina, el Caribe, España y Portugal |url=https://www.latindex.org/latindex/nosotros/descripcion |access-date=2022-04-11 |website=www.latindex.org}}</ref> It began as a database of academic journals in Latin America, including ones that were no longer active or focused on scientific communication. The database also established criteria to define what makes a quality journal, based on the historical, cultural, and scientific context of the region, supporting and promoting scientific publication in regional languages.<ref name=":9" />

Currently, Cetto Kramis is part of the foundation board of the [[Directory of Open Access Journals]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Foundation Board & Advisory Board – DOAJ |url=https://doaj.org/about/advisory-board-council/ |access-date=2026-03-12 |website=doaj.org |language=en}}</ref> She serves as the chair of [[UNESCO]]'s Scientific Diplomacy & Scientific Heritage,<ref>{{Cite web |title=About us – UNESCO Science Diplomacy and Scientific Heritage |url=https://unescochair-sdh.org/about-us/ |access-date=2026-03-12 |language=en-US}}</ref> and contributed to the creation of recommendations from UNESCO’s Open Science Committee, which were published in 2021.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Open science |url=https://www.unesco.org/en/open-science |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260223030628/https://www.unesco.org/en/open-science |archive-date=2026-02-23 |access-date=2026-03-12 |language=en}}</ref>

=== Museum of Light ===
Cetto Kramis participated in the project focused on the creation of the [[Museum of Light, Mexico City|Museum of Light]] in Mexico City. The Museum of Light is a thematic museum of the General Directorate for the Dissemination of Science of UNAM, and was inaugurated in 1996.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2017-01-16 |title="Museo de la Luz, único en su tipo en el mundo": Ana María Cetto |url=https://www.cronica.com.mx/notas-“museo_de_la_luz_unico_en_su_tipo_en_el_mundo”_ana_maria_cetto-1004920-2017 |access-date=2022-04-11 |website=www.cronica.com.mx/ |language=es}}</ref> Cetto Kramis was in charge of its renovation in 2016.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2016-11-22 |title=🔊Ana María Cetto y el Museo de la Luz, una historia en común {{!}} UNAM Global |url=https://unamglobal.unam.mx/🔊ana-maria-cetto-y-el-museo-de-la-luz-una-historia-en-comun/ |access-date=2022-04-11 |language=es}}</ref> She was also a promoter of the International Year of Light 2015 and belongs to the International Steering Committee of the International Day of Light.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Barreiro |first=Luis Juan López |date=2018-06-04 |title=La LUZ ya tiene su día {{!}} Iluminet revista de iluminación |url=https://www.iluminet.com/dia-internacional-luz-unesco/ |access-date=2022-04-11 |language=es}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=UNESCO Endorses International Day of Light |url=https://spie.org/news/spie-professional-magazine-archive/2017-january/unesco-endorses-international-day-of-light |access-date=2022-04-11 |website=spie.org}}</ref>

=== Quantum Research ===
Cetto Kramis has made many contributions to the field of quantum mechanics in recent years. In 2022 she published a paper explaining the role of vacuum fields in quantum mechanics.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Cetto |first1=Ana Maria |last2=de la Peña |first2=Luis |date=2022-11-24 |title=The Electromagnetic Vacuum Field as an Essential Hidden Ingredient of the Quantum-Mechanical Ontology |journal=Entropy |language=en |volume=24 |issue=12 |pages=1717 |doi=10.3390/e24121717 |doi-access=free |issn=1099-4300 |pmc=9777925 |pmid=36554122 |arxiv=2210.16388 |bibcode=2022Entrp..24.1717C }}</ref> She also contributed to the derivation of fundamental commutation relations.<ref name=":9" />

Working closely with her husband Luis de la Peña, Cetto Kramis authored many papers on foundational quantum mechanics after her attempts to study biophysics and photosynthesis at the [[Consejo Nacional de Ciencia y Tecnologia]] in 1970. In 1971, she defended her doctoral thesis entitled ''Investigaciones sobre una teoría estocástica de la mecánica cuántica'' (Investigations of a stochastics theory of quantum mechanics)<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Cetto Kramis |first=Ana Maria |date=1971 |title=Investigaciones sobre una teoría estocástica de la mecánica cuántica |url=https://hdl.handle.net/20.500.14330/TES01000650052 |journal=Universidad Nacional Autónoma de México |hdl=20.500.14330/TES01000650052 }}</ref> and became the first woman to earn a Ph.D. in physics in Mexico.<ref name=":9" />

From 2008 to 2021, Cetto Kramis and De la Peña published many papers with co-author Andrea Valdés-Hernández, one of de la Peña's former Ph.D. students. Valdés-Hernández made noteworthy contributions to their studies on [[quantum entanglement]].<ref name=":9" />

== Awards and honors ==
Ana María Cetto Kramis's work has been related to the [[Nobel Peace Prize]] on two different occasions. While on the council of [[Pugwash Conferences]] in 1995, the organization received the Nobel Peace Prize.<ref name=":1" /> The prize was granted for "their efforts to diminish the part played by nuclear arms in international politics and, in the longer run, to eliminate such arms".<ref>{{Cite web |title=The Nobel Peace Prize 1995 |url=https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/peace/1995/press-release/ |access-date=2022-04-11 |website=NobelPrize.org |language=en-US}}</ref> From 2003 to 2010 she was deputy director general and head of the technical cooperation department of the [[International Atomic Energy Agency]] (IAEA) dedicated to the control of the proliferation of nuclear weapons.<ref name=":2" /> The IAEA was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize in 2005 for "their effort to prevent nuclear energy from being used for military purposes and to ensure that nuclear energy for peaceful purposes is used in the safest possible way".<ref>{{Cite web |title=The Nobel Peace Prize 2005 |url=https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/peace/2005/press-release/ |access-date=2022-04-11 |website=NobelPrize.org |language=en-US}}</ref>

Ana María Cetto Kramis's work has been recognized with several other distinctions, including the following:

* Honorary doctorate from the [[Tajik National University]] (2007)<ref name=":8" />
* Second place in the Award for Mexican Women Inventors and Innovators for the Latindex Project (2008)<ref name=":3">{{Cite journal |last=Unam |first=Comunidad |date=2008-10-20 |title=PREMIAN A ANA MARÍA CETTO POR LA CREACIÓN DEL LATINDEX |url=http://acervo.gaceta.unam.mx/index.php/gum00/article/view/60727 |journal=Gaceta UNAM (2000-2009) |language=es-ES |issue=3946 |pages=3}}</ref>
* Juchimán Silver Prize in Science and Technology 2010, Mexico, (2011)<ref name=":5">{{Cite web |title=Ana María Cetto reconocida con el premio Juchiman de Plata 2010 |url=http://www.fisica.unam.mx/noticias.php?id=63 |access-date=2022-04-11 |website=Instituto de Física, UNAM |language=es}}</ref>

* Selected as one of the thirteen women for the "Woman and Science: 13 Names to Change the World" Exhibition (2013)<ref>{{Cite web |title=Mujer y Ciencia: 13 nombres para cambiar el mundo |url=https://fciencias.ugr.es/34-noticias/2252-mujer-y-ciencia-13-nombres-para-cambiar-el-mundo |access-date=2022-04-11 |website=Facultad de Ciencias |date=7 March 2016 |language=es-es}}</ref>
* Included among the 50 most outstanding women in Mexico by ''Forbes México'' magazine (2015)<ref name=":6">{{Cite web |last=Staff |first=Forbes |date=2015-06-19 |title=5 mujeres poderosas e inesperadas de México |url=https://www.forbes.com.mx/5-mujeres-poderosas-e-inesperadas-de-mexico/ |access-date=2022-04-11 |website=Forbes México |language=es}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
Cetto currently resides in Mexico City and was married to her long time mentor from the [[National Autonomous University of Mexico]] (UNAM), physicist [[Luis de la Peña]], until his death in 2026. They had one daughter.<ref name=":9" /><ref>{{cite web | title=El Correo Ilustrado | publisher=La Jornada | date=April 18, 2018 | url=https://www.jornada.com.mx/2018/04/18/opinion/002a2cor | language=es | access-date=September 8, 2026}}</ref>
